title: Pontotoc court records go offline Dec. 23. Here’s where to file on paper
excerpt: Pontotoc County’s chancery and circuit clerks will accept paper filings during regular office hours while the state moves court records into new judicial districts.
locality: Pontotoc County chancery and circuit courts in Mississippi.

facts.statement: People who need a Pontotoc County chancery or circuit court record before the end of December have until 5 p.m. Wednesday, Dec. 23, to retrieve it electronically. The state judiciary says the shutdown will take out both online access and the public terminals at the courthouse. Clerks will also lose access to the electronic records.

facts.statement: The state Supreme Court’s Nov. 4 order calls for paper filings at the appropriate clerk’s office during its regular business hours. Clerks will stamp documents when they arrive and use that filing date when they enter them in the system later.

paragraphs.text: People who need a Pontotoc County chancery or circuit court record before the end of December have until 5 p.m. Wednesday, Dec. 23, to retrieve it electronically. The state judiciary says the shutdown will take out both online access and the public terminals at the courthouse. Clerks will also lose access to the electronic records.

The state Supreme Court’s Nov. 4 order calls for paper filings at the appropriate clerk’s office during its regular business hours. The four business days the state identifies during the outage are Monday, Dec. 28, through Thursday, Dec. 31. Clerks will stamp documents when they arrive and use that filing date when they enter them in the system later.

For questions about a local filing or office hours, the Pontotoc County circuit clerk’s number is 662-489-3908. The chancery clerk can be reached at 662-489-3900. Those are the numbers in the Mississippi secretary of state’s county directory.

The outage gives the state time to move cases, documents and users into judicial districts that take effect Jan. 1. The planned restart is 8 a.m. Monday, Jan. 4. The Supreme Court order says the outage ends when the Administrative Office of Courts announces service has returned at mec.ms.gov. Electronic filing in the appellate courts will remain available.
